produce an ordered sequence of steps that describe a solution of the problem

slides.title: Problem solving phase

blocks.text: The central concept underlying all computation is that of the algorithm
an algorithm is a step-by-step sequence of instructions for carrying out some task.
The algorithm is a conceptual solution
The technical solution is the program implementing the algorithm.

slides.title: Steps in Problem Solving

blocks.text: First produce a general algorithm (one can use pseudocode)
Refine the algorithm successively to get step by step detailed algorithm that is very close to a computer language.
Pseudocode is an artificial and informal language that helps programmers develop algorithms.

slides.title: Implementation phase

blocks.text: Programming can be viewed as the process of designing and implementing algorithms that a computer can carry out.
create an algorithm for accomplishing a given objective, then

slides.raw_text:
Implementation phase 
Programming can be viewed as the process of designing and 
implementing algorithms that a computer can carry out.
A programmer’s job is to: 
create an algorithm for accomplishing a given objective, then 
translate the individual steps of the algorithm into a 
programming language that the computer can understand

slides.title: The Flowchart

blocks.text: A schematic representation of a sequence of operations, as in a manufacturing process or computer program.
A graphical representation of the sequence of operations in an information system or program.
Information system flowcharts show how data flows from source documents through the computer to final distribution to users.
Program flowcharts show the sequence of instructions in a single program or subroutine.
Different symbols are used to draw each type of flowchart.

slides.raw_text:
The Flowchart
A schematic representation of a sequence of operations, as 
in a manufacturing process or computer program.
A graphical representation of the sequence of operations in 
an information system or program. 
Information system flowcharts show how data flows from 
source documents through the computer to final distribution to 
users. 
Program flowcharts show the sequence of instructions in a 
single program or subroutine. 
Different symbols are used to draw each type of flowchart.
